title: How One Hardcoded Key Leaked Everything

scenes.narration: This single hardcoded AWS key cost a startup forty thousand dollars in thirty minutes.
scenes.headline: 40K Burned in 30 Minutes
scenes.subline: How one commit turned an AWS account into a public crypto miner.

scenes.narration: A junior engineer accidentally committed production AWS credentials directly into a public GitHub repository.
scenes.headline: Production Keys in Git
scenes.subline: Scraping bots cloned the repository within four seconds of the push.

scenes.narration: Automated scrapers indexed the keys instantly and spun up four hundred GPU instances before the alarm even fired.
scenes.headline: 400 GPUs in 60 Seconds
scenes.subline: The bots didn't even read the code.

scenes.narration: The immediate fix is revoking the IAM credential and switching to short-lived OpenID Connect role federation.
scenes.headline: Revoke and Rotate Immediately
scenes.subline: Never store static cloud keys in source control.

lines.t: Switching deployment pipeline to AWS OIDC...

scenes.narration: Always use GitHub OIDC tokens and IAM roles. Never use long-lived root keys.
scenes.headline: Kill Static IAM Keys
scenes.subline: Temporary STS tokens eliminate leakage risks forever.
